title: Retry failed refunds with backoff
summary: Failed refunds now retry with growing, random waits and stop after 5 attempts. Retries can no longer refund a customer twice.

steps.title: The problem
steps.body:
Before this change, a failed refund retried every 60 seconds, forever.
- A gateway outage caused a flood of retries.
- A retry after a timeout could refund the customer twice.
- Some errors can never succeed, for example a closed card.

terms.meaning: Money that goes back to the customer for a payment.
One try to send a refund to the gateway.
A wait between attempts that grows after each failure.
Randomness in the wait, so retries do not all start at the same time.
An id that lets the gateway ignore a request it already did.
An error that can succeed if you try again later.

steps.title: Parts of the refund flow
steps.say: A worker picks due refunds. The retry logic talks to the gateway and records the result in the store.

notes.text: The worker asks the store for refunds that are due now.
retryRefund sends one attempt to the gateway.
The result goes back to the store: done, failed, or retry later.

steps.say: Follow one refund from the worker to the gateway and back.

messages.note: Count this attempt before we send it.

messages.note: The refund id goes along as the idempotency key.

steps.title: Check
steps.question: Why does each retry wait a random time?

options.text: So that many retries do not hit the gateway at the same moment.
options.why: Correct. Jitter spreads retries over time after an outage.

options.text: So that the gateway cannot guess when the next retry comes.
options.why: No. This is not a security measure.

options.text: Because the gateway requires random waits between refunds.
options.why: No. The gateway has no such rule. The change protects the gateway from load.

options.text: To keep the total retry time under 60 seconds.
options.why: No. The waits grow with each attempt and can be much longer.

steps.title: One retry attempt
steps.say: The worker counts the attempt, then retryRefund sends it and records the result.

notes.text: The attempt count goes up first. If the process crashes during the call, the attempt still counts.
Before: every failure waited a fixed 60 seconds and retried forever.
nextDelay picks a random wait up to a cap. The cap doubles after each attempt.
The refund id is the idempotency key. A repeated call cannot refund the customer twice.
A retryable failure schedules the next attempt with the new backoff.

steps.title: Check
steps.question: A gateway call times out, but the gateway did process the refund. What happens on the next attempt?

options.text: The gateway sees the same idempotency key and does not refund again.
options.why: Correct. The key makes the repeated call safe.

options.text: The worker skips the refund because the attempt count went up.
options.why: No. The count only stops retries after 5 attempts.

options.text: The customer gets a second refund, which support must reverse.
options.why: No. That was the old behavior. The key now prevents it.

steps.title: When to give up
steps.say: Two new rules stop retries that cannot succeed.

notes.text: After 5 attempts, the refund is marked failed with reason max_attempts.
A non-retryable error, for example a closed card, fails the refund at once.

steps.title: Where retryable comes from
steps.say: The gateway client decides if an error is retryable.

notes.text: Each gateway error carries a code and a retryable flag. This PR does not change it, but the retry logic now depends on it.

steps.title: Non-retryable error
steps.say: A closed card fails the refund at the first attempt.

messages.label: card_closed
messages.note: retryable is false for this code.

steps.title: Check
steps.question: A refund fails with a retryable error on its 5th attempt. What happens?

options.text: It is marked failed with reason max_attempts on the next run.
options.why: Correct. A 6th retry is scheduled, and the check at the top stops it.

options.text: It is marked failed at once with the gateway error code.
options.why: No. Only non-retryable errors fail at once.
No. The attempt limit stops it.

options.text: The worker resets the attempt count to 0.

steps.title: What to check
steps.body:
- Is 5 attempts the right limit for all payment methods?
- Does every gateway error set `retryable` correctly?
- The attempt count goes up before the call. Is that the intended order?

steps.title: In short
steps.body:
- Waits grow and are random.
- Retries stop after 5 attempts.
- Errors that cannot succeed fail at once.
- The idempotency key prevents double refunds.
